headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Airbyte has broad network egress while Marker is local-only, creating a default path for sensitive business data to leave the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can ingest external data and Marker processes documents, so a prompt-injection-style bridge is plausible if Airbyte outputs are manually or file-fed into Marker. However, Marker has no shared channel or parser surface documented, and both profiles lack a default direct handoff. The pathway is possible but not strong.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into Marker as document content
IF a shared workspace or manual copy-paste bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Disable any copy-paste handoff between Airbyte outputs and Marker inputs
Use a strict content sanitizer before passing text to Marker
Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Add a human review step for any instruction-like text in documents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, while Marker is local-only with no network egress. If Airbyte forwards sensitive business data into Marker-derived outputs or logs, the pair can expose data through Airbyte's outbound paths. The blast radius is more than one document, but the profiles do not show uncontrolled third-party upload by Marker.
conditions: IF business data processed by Airbyte is included in Marker inputs or outputs
IF Airbyte sends those outputs to an external API or destination
mitigations: Restrict Airbyte connectors to non-sensitive datasets
Turn off any outbound destinations not required for the workflow
Redact sensitive fields before Marker processes documents
Review Airbyte destination settings before each run
Keep Marker offline from any shared export path

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and API access, while Marker is explicitly unable to write files, modify git state, or use network. That means direct write-write conflict is limited. A conflict could still arise if both are pointed at the same external resource through Airbyte's APIs, but the documented overlap is narrow.
conditions: IF both agents are configured against the same mutable external API or dataset
IF Airbyte is granted write access to a shared downstream system
mitigations: Assign separate destinations to each agent
Avoid concurrent writes to the same external resource
Use per-agent service accounts
Add a manual lock or queue before shared updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data, and Marker can consume documents, so A's output can become B's input. Marker has no documented verification or critique surface, so if it renders Airbyte-produced content as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream documents. The pair lacks evidence of a built-in validation step.
conditions: IF Marker is fed Airbyte-generated documents without a verification step
IF downstream users treat Marker output as authoritative
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Airbyte and Marker
Require source citations in Marker outputs
Compare sampled outputs against the original Airbyte records
Flag any transformed fields for human review

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, while Marker is local-only and shows no special compliance claims or sensitive data classes. The pair suggests a possible retention or residency mismatch only if regulated business data is routed through Airbyte into Marker workflows. No direct residency conflict is documented, so this remains a limited compliance gap.
conditions: IF regulated business data is routed through Airbyte into Marker
IF retention or residency rules differ between the Airbyte destination and Marker storage
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it through the pair
Keep regulated datasets out of the workflow
Document retention settings for both tools
Delete temporary Marker artifacts after use
